gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ASUS's own pages limit its ZenScreen Duo on a Mac to one screen in Extend mode. ChatGPT showed that two-screen unit as its "best value" pick at $249.99. ASUS's ZenScreen Duo OLED FAQ says Mac shows only the lower screen and "cannot display on the upper screen" in Extend mode, and the MB14FCD page footnotes that a MacBook's USB-C port "only supports extended mode for a single external display". So a MacBook trader gets one extra chart screen, not two.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. Macworld's best portable monitors for Mac (Simon Jary, updated 2026-10-16) is the only rival ChatGPT cited. It covers only the Trio 3 Pro and KYY X90G, says base M1 and M2 Macs need Mobile Pixels' software, and never mentions the ZenScreen Duo. deskgearhq's 2026 guide lists the ZenScreen Duo MB14FCD and marks macOS as supported for all five products. It also says every unit runs over a single USB-C cable using DisplayPort Alt Mode and has no Mac caveat. itechguides' 2026 list says Mac support "cannot be reduced to yes or no" but has no ZenScreen Duo entry and says nothing about single-cable Extend on Mac. Xebec's help page talks about ports, not Mac chips. No rival names the base M3, which Apple limits to one external display while the lid is open. That decides the pick for MacBook shoppers. ChatGPT itself asks "What laptop do you use? MacBook". It does not change the pick for Windows laptops.
decides: For a Mac trader who wants two added screens: (1) The ASUS ZenScreen Duo drops out as a two-screen option over one cable, because by ASUS's own documents it extends to one screen on a Mac. (2) The Trio 3 Pro runs both screens without a driver only on a laptop with two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports. On a base M1 or M2 Mac it needs Mobile Pixels' software, according to the manual as Macworld's review quotes it. Apple's spec for the M3 MacBook Air allows one external display with the lid open, so the base M3 belongs in the software group too, which Macworld does not say. An M4 MacBook Air drives two external displays natively. This confirms the Trio 3 Pro as the Mac pick, with the chip caveat stated. Our own FOPO S1, S7, S10 and S11 are sold as "driver-free" two-screen units. If they also drive both screens from one USB-C cable, they may hit the same Mac Extend limit. Check FOPO's own document before the page says they run two screens on a Mac.

findings.label: Extend across both screens from a MacBook
findings.value: One screen only. ASUS footnote: a MacBook's Type-C port "only supports extended mode for a single external display"
findings.source_title: ASUS ZenScreen Duo MB14FCD I 360° Foldable Portable Monitor
findings.note: This is the Extend-mode footnote on ASUS's US product page. Whatever the footnote's exact wording about the Mac setup, its point is that a MacBook extends to one screen. The same page says "A single USB-C cable is all that's required to duplicate or extend a laptop screen" and that Extend needs the USB-C2 port. This is the 14-inch 1920×1200 IPS ZenScreen Duo that ChatGPT showed at $249.99.

findings.label: Video path and Mac driver
findings.value: Native USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode, no macOS driver. Needs a laptop USB-C port with DP Alt Mode; otherwise mini-HDMI for video plus separate USB-C power
findings.source_title: ASUS ZenScreen Duo MB14FCD I 360° Foldable Portable Monitor
findings.note: ASUS FAQ on the page: "compatible with most MacBooks that support USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode" and "No additional drivers are needed for macOS". Footnote: "All MacBooks with Thunderbolt 3, Thunderbolt 4, Thunderbolt 5, or USB4 ports support DisplayPort Alt Mode." The HDMI port does not support DisplayWidget Center, so auto-rotate is off over HDMI.

findings.label: Extend mode on a Mac
findings.value: Lower screen (A2) only. ASUS: "MAC / Chrome OS / phone only support lower screen (A2) display, cannot display on the upper screen (A1)"
findings.source_title: [OLED Monitor] ZenScreen DUO OLED Multiple Display Settings and Connection Methods Introduction
findings.note: ASUS support FAQ, last updated 2025-03-04. It also says Extend mode "only supports Type C 2 interfaces" and "HDMI does not support extend mode". The FAQ's table of supported systems is an image and could not be read. This FAQ covers the OLED sibling, not the MB14FCD; it backs up the MB14FCD footnote.

findings.label: When no driver is needed
findings.value: Only on a laptop with two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports, one cable per screen. Running both screens from one cable needs Mobile Pixels' software
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Jary quotes the manual: "if your laptop has two DP enabled USB-C ports … driver installation is not necessary". The software is also needed to run both screens from a single cable and to get full brightness with a power adapter. Two 0.5 m USB-C cables come in the box. Tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro. A power adapter on one of the Trio's USB-C ports passes up to 65 W through to the laptop.

findings.label: Macs that need the software
findings.value: Base (non-Pro/Max) M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo need free Mobile Pixels software "rather like DisplayLink". Jary says M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and any M4/M5 MacBook should be fine without it
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: This is the reviewer's statement, not a Mobile Pixels document; mobilepixels.us returned HTTP 429. Macworld's best-of page (updated 2026-10-16, cited by ChatGPT) says the same for M1 and M2 and does not name the base M3.

findings.label: Base M3 MacBook Air: external displays with lid open
findings.value: 1 external display (up to 6K 60 Hz). A second works only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple: "Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display". A screen extender needs the lid open, so a base M3 Air natively runs one added screen. Inference: like base M1 and M2, it needs a driver (such as Mobile Pixels' software) for two added screens.

findings.label: M4 MacBook Air: external displays
findings.value: Up to two external displays (up to 6K 60 Hz) alongside the built-in display. Native DisplayPort 1.4 over USB-C
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple: "Simultaneously supports full native resolution on the built-in display … and: Up to two external displays". So two added screens on one cable each, with no driver.

findings.label: Fit range and video path
findings.value: Fits 13–18-inch laptops (Xebec's range). USB-C with DisplayPort, DP Alt Mode or Thunderbolt 3+ needs no adapter. A power-only or USB 3.2 Gen 1 USB-C port needs a mini HDMI to HDMI cable. USB-A-only laptops also need a USB-A to USB-C converter
findings.source_title: What laptops are compatible with the Dual-Screen 3? (Xebec Help Center)
findings.note: Xebec says it "supports all operating systems, including Mac, Windows, ChromeOS, and Linux" and that the Dual-Screen 3 "does not need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter". The page names no Mac chip limits and no DisplayLink.
